questions.question_text: Which sequence of transformations maps $y = f(x)$ onto $y = f(2x - 10)$?

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$, then translation $5$ units to the right
Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$, then translation $10$ units to the right
options.why: Did not factor $2$ out of the bracket before finding the horizontal translation.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $2$, then translation $5$ units to the right
options.why: Used a horizontal dilation factor of $2$ instead of $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$, then translation $5$ units to the left
options.why: Shifted to the left instead of to the right for $x - 5$.

questions.solution_text:
$y = f(2(x - 5))$
$\text{Horizontal dilation by factor } \dfrac{1}{2}, \text{ then translation } 5 \text{ units to the right}$

questions.question_text: Which sequence of transformations maps $y = f(x)$ onto $y = f(7x + 21)$?

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{7}$, then translation $3$ units to the left
Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{7}$, then translation $21$ units to the left
options.why: Forgot to factor $7$ out of $21$ when finding the horizontal shift.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $7$, then translation $3$ units to the left
options.why: Used a horizontal dilation factor of $7$ instead of the reciprocal $\dfrac{1}{7}$.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{7}$, then translation $3$ units to the right
options.why: Translated to the right instead of to the left for $x + 3$.

questions.solution_text:
$y = f(7(x + 3))$
$\text{Horizontal dilation by factor } \dfrac{1}{7}, \text{ then translation } 3 \text{ units to the left}$

options.text: Horizontal translation $2$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $5$, vertical translation $8$ units up
Horizontal translation $2$ units left, vertical dilation by factor $5$, vertical translation $8$ units up
options.why: Shifted to the left instead of to the right for $(x - 2)$.

options.text: Horizontal translation $2$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{5}$, vertical translation $8$ units up
options.why: Used a vertical dilation factor of $\dfrac{1}{5}$ instead of $5$.

options.text: Horizontal translation $2$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $5$, vertical translation $8$ units down
options.why: Shifted down instead of up for $+8$.

questions.solution_text:
$y = 5(x - 2)^2 + 8$
$\text{Horizontal translation } 2 \text{ units right, vertical dilation factor } 5, \text{ vertical translation } 8 \text{ units up}$

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{3}$, translation $2$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $4$, translation $2$ units up
Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{3}$, translation $6$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $4$, translation $2$ units up
options.why: Did not factor $3$ from the bracket, taking $6$ as the horizontal shift.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $3$, translation $2$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $4$, translation $2$ units up
options.why: Used a horizontal dilation factor of $3$ instead of $\dfrac{1}{3}$.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{3}$, translation $2$ units left, vertical dilation by factor $4$, translation $2$ units up
options.why: Shifted left instead of right for $x - 2$.

questions.solution_text:
$y = 4f(3(x - 2)) + 2$
$\text{Horizontal dilation by } \dfrac{1}{3}, \text{ translation } 2 \text{ units right, vertical dilation by } 4, \text{ translation } 2 \text{ units up}$

options.text: Translation $5$ units left, vertical dilation by factor $3$, reflection in $x$-axis, translation $9$ units down
Translation $5$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $3$, reflection in $x$-axis, translation $9$ units down
options.why: Read $f(x + 5)$ as a shift of $5$ units right, taking the sign of the $+5$ at face value instead of solving $x + 5 = 0$.

options.text: Translation $5$ units left, vertical dilation by factor $3$, reflection in $y$-axis, translation $9$ units down
options.why: Attached the negative sign in $-3f(\ldots)$ to the input, so the reflection was taken in the $y$-axis (as for $f(-x)$) instead of the $x$-axis.

options.text: Translation $5$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $3$, reflection in $y$-axis, translation $9$ units down
options.why: Made both slips: read $+5$ as a shift right, and treated the outside negative as a reflection in the $y$-axis rather than the $x$-axis.

questions.solution_text:
$y = -3f(x + 5) - 9$
$\text{Translation } 5 \text{ units left, vertical dilation by } 3, \text{ reflection in } x\text{-axis, translation } 9 \text{ units down}$

questions.question_text: Which transformations map $y = f(x)$ onto $y = f(7 - x)$?

options.text: Reflection in the $y$-axis, then translation $7$ units to the right
Reflection in the $y$-axis, then translation $7$ units to the left
options.why: Factored as $-(x - 7)$ but shifted left instead of right.

options.text: Reflection in the $x$-axis, then translation $7$ units to the right
options.why: Identified a reflection in the $x$-axis instead of the $y$-axis.

options.text: Translation $7$ units to the right with no reflection
options.why: Ignored the negative sign attached to $x$ inside the function argument.

questions.solution_text:
$y = f(-(x - 7))$
$\text{Reflection in } y\text{-axis, then translation } 7 \text{ units to the right}$

questions.question_text: What is the horizontal translation when $y = f(x)$ is transformed to $y = f(6x - 24)$?

options.text: $4$ units to the right
$24$ units to the right
options.why: Used the unfactored constant $24$ without dividing by the coefficient $6$.

options.text: $4$ units to the left
options.why: Interpreted the subtraction as a shift to the left.

options.text: $24$ units to the left
options.why: Did not divide by $6$ and shifted in the wrong direction.

questions.question_text: What is the vertical dilation factor in the transformation $y = \dfrac{f(4x - 8)}{5} + 3$?

options.why: Took the denominator as a multiplier factor rather than its reciprocal.
Confused the horizontal dilation factor with the vertical dilation factor.
Mistook the vertical translation constant for the dilation factor.

questions.question_text: Describe the complete transformation sequence mapping $y = \sqrt{x}$ onto $y = -4\sqrt{8 - 2x} + 5$.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$, reflection in $y$-axis, translation $4$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $4$, reflection in $x$-axis, translation $5$ units up
Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$, reflection in $y$-axis, translation $8$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $4$, reflection in $x$-axis, translation $5$ units up
options.why: Did not factor $2$ out of $8$ inside the radical expression.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $2$, reflection in $y$-axis, translation $4$ units right, vertical dilation by factor $4$, reflection in $x$-axis, translation $5$ units up
options.why: Used a horizontal dilation factor of $2$ instead of $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

options.text: Horizontal dilation by factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$, reflection in $y$-axis, translation $4$ units left, vertical dilation by factor $4$, reflection in $x$-axis, translation $5$ units up
options.why: Shifted left instead of right for $x - 4$.

questions.solution_text:
$y = -4\sqrt{-2(x - 4)} + 5$
$\text{Horizontal dilation by } \dfrac{1}{2}, \text{ reflection in } y\text{-axis, translation } 4 \text{ units right, vertical dilation by } 4, \text{ reflection in } x\text{-axis, translation } 5 \text{ units up}$

questions.question_text: By writing $y = 4x^2 - 24x + 19$ in the form $y = a(x - h)^2 + k$, determine the horizontal and vertical translations from $y = x^2$.

options.text: Translation $3$ units to the right and $17$ units down
Translation $3$ units to the left and $17$ units down
options.why: Interpreted $(x - 3)^2$ as a shift $3$ units to the left, reading the sign inside the bracket directly instead of solving $x - 3 = 0$.

options.text: Translation $3$ units to the right and $10$ units up
options.why: Forgot to multiply the completed-square constant by the factor $4$, writing $4(x - 3)^2 - 9 + 19 = 4(x - 3)^2 + 10$ instead of subtracting $36$.

options.text: Translation $3$ units to the left and $10$ units up
options.why: Made both slips: subtracted only $9$ rather than $4 \times 9 = 36$, giving $+10$, and read $(x - 3)^2$ as a shift to the left.
